title: Latency Meshboard: split streaming vs non-streaming by model and route
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a new 'Latency Meshboard' that decomposes p50/p95/p99 latency across model, route, and I/O mode with explicit streaming vs non-streaming (blocking) splits. This ticket covers schema changes, tracing hooks, metric derivation, dashboard panels, and an acceptance rollout plan. The goal is a single, shareable board for SRE/Platform/Runtime teams that surfaces where tail latency is coming from (serve time, batching, kernel stalls, network) and how streaming semantics change the measurements.
acceptance_criteria: New metric 'redwood.serve_latency_ms' emitted with labels: model_family, model_version, route, io_mode (streaming|blocking), region, request_shape
Tracing spans include span attribute 'io.mode' and 'route.id' for all runtime entrypoints and stream frames where applicable
Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 heatmap by (model_family x route) with a toggle that splits series into streaming vs blocking and shows delta columns

Streaming measurements use stream_end latency (time from request start to first/last chunk as defined) while blocking uses end-to-end completion latency; both computed consistently in metrics pipeline
Panels have linked trace drilldowns for selected cohort (e.g., p99 streaming on model X -> opens trace with servepath hooks)
Automated alerting rule added for p99 > configured baseline by model-route-io_mode with suppression for low-volume cohorts
design_decisions: Emit a single histogram metric 'redwood.serve_latency_ms' and derive pXX via the metrics backend (ClickHouse/Prometheus adaptor). Rationale: single source simplifies rollups and avoids duplication

Tracing: add lightweight span annotation at kernel-scheduler, batching, and network boundary points. We'll reuse existing trace IDs and add 'io.mode' and 'request.shape' tags to avoid costly re-instrumentation

Sampling: increase trace sampling to 1% for production by default and 5% for routes flagged as high-risk (configurable). For p99 investigations, rely on linked traces from aggregated telemetry rather than full traffic sampling

Streaming semantics: treat 'streaming' as first-chunk latency and 'stream_end' as last-chunk latency. Dashboard will expose both 'stream-first' and 'stream-end' but default to 'stream-end' for tail analysis since user-perceived completion matters for SLOs
Query performance: pre-aggregate 1m buckets for high-cardinality labels (model_version excluded from default view) to keep dashboard load under 1s for typical queries
implementation_steps: 1) Add span attributes and minimal trace hooks in runtime entry path and in stream frame writer (PR runtime#3487)
2) Emit 'io.mode' label on HTTP entrypoints and SDK wrappers; backfill producer code for Websocket/GRPC streaming paths
3) Update metrics ingestion pipeline to accept new histogram and derive p50/p95/p99; add transform to tag streaming vs blocking correctly
4) Create ClickHouse/Metrics views for model_family x route x io_mode heatmap and pre-aggregated buckets
5) Build Grafana/Console panels: overview grid, delta comparator (stream vs blocking), trace-linked flyout, and cohort builder
6) Add SLO-based alerts and a runbook entry for investigating p99 streaming anomalies
7) Synthetic test: run workload harness to produce controlled streaming and blocking loads to validate metrics and traces
8) Phased rollout: internal-only -> beta customers -> global rollout with monitoring
telemetry_queries: ClickHouse example for p95: SELECT model_family, route, io_mode, quantileExact(0.95)(value) as p95 FROM metrics_serve_latency WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY model_family, route, io_mode
PromQL example for p99 approximation (histogram_quantile): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_serve_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family, route, io_mode))

Streaming-first vs streaming-end: derive two series: 'stream_first_latency_ms' (first_chunk_timestamp - request_start) and 'stream_end_latency_ms' (last_chunk_timestamp - request_start). Ensure ingestion attaches chunk timestamps to trace/metric events
Volume guard: only compute p99 for cohorts with >= 100 samples in the window; otherwise annotate as 'low volume'
Trace link query: surface top N traces where serve_latency_ms in top percentile and include trace_id in dashboard link
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): run full stack locally with synthetic harness and unit tests for label emission
Phase 1 (internal): enable in canary fleet with metrics/trace TTL 7d and validate panels with runtime/observability leads
Phase 2 (beta): enable for 10% of production routes (non-critical customers) - gather p50/p95/p99 baselines and adjust pre-aggregation windows
Phase 3 (GA): global enable with dashboard added to Console -> Observability -> Latency Meshboard. Announce in #platform-observability
Fallback: if metric ingestion errors exceed threshold, revert to previous metric name and open incident (see runbook)
testing_notes: Create synthetic scenario generator that produces streaming sessions with staggered chunk times to simulate network jitter and tail kernel stalls
Validate that tracing hooks capture batching boundary spans and kernel scheduling stalls by asserting span attributes and durations in test traces
Compare metrics-derived p95 with sampled raw trace durations for a 24h window to ensure < 5% divergence
Load test dashboard queries at expected cardinality to keep panel render < 2s; iterate on pre-aggregation if needed
